title: Annotate it for your evidence portfolio
why_matters: A piece of work without annotation is a document. With annotation — what you did, what changed, what you'd do differently — it's evidence of judgement. The annotation is what your line manager will read; the document itself they'll skim. Write the annotation as if the rest of the work were optional.
steps: Use the probation-pack playbook's evidence portfolio structure: what it was, what you did, what changed, what you'd do differently.
Write each section in one or two sentences. Resist the urge to lavish. The discipline is in the cutting.
Add links / file references to the actual artefacts. Make it scannable.
Show it to your line manager in your next 1:1 (or send ahead if their preference). Ask one question: "is this the version you'd want to see in the review?".
success_criteria: The portfolio entry exists in the probation-pack format. It is one screen long. Your line manager has reviewed it and either endorsed or amended.
reflection_prompt: What did your manager react to that you didn't expect, and what does it tell you about how they read evidence?
